packs.name: jdk
packs.about: Java 21, which Gradle, sdkmanager and the emulator tools need. The first thing a node needs for Android work.

packs.name: android-tools
packs.about: sdkmanager and avdmanager, through which every other Android toolchain installs. Sets this node's ANDROID_HOME.

packs.name: android-cmake
packs.about: The CMake the NDK's build system uses.

packs.name: android-emulator
packs.about: The Android emulator. Its system images, one per API level, are added on the Emulator tab. Google ships it for x86_64 Linux only.

packs.name: android-platform-tools
packs.about: adb and the other tools that talk to a phone or an emulator; the emulator and the Phone tab need it. Google ships it for x86_64 Linux only.

packs.name: android-platforms
packs.about: The android.jar a build compiles against (compileSdk), at the newest level Google publishes. Update adds the next level beside it, so older projects keep building. Removing this removes every level.

packs.name: android-build-tools
packs.about: aapt2, d8, zipalign and apksigner at the newest stable version. Update adds the next beside it.

packs.name: android-ndk
packs.about: Native development kit, for C and C++ inside an Android app.

packs.name: flutter
packs.about: Flutter with its Dart SDK. Builds Android apps on Linux, and iOS too on a Mac with Xcode.

packs.name: go
packs.about: Go, which cross-compiles to Windows, macOS, Linux and ARM with nothing else to install.

packs.name: dotnet
packs.about: The .NET SDK plus the maui-android workload: Android apps from C#.

packs.name: node
packs.about: Node.js and npm, for a project built with npm and for anything that drives a browser with Playwright.

packs.name: python
packs.about: uv and a Python 3.12 with pip and venv, for a project's own dependencies: uv venv, then uv pip install -r requirements.txt. The node's own python3 has neither.

packs.name: playwright
packs.about: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with the module that drives them, for aerie capture shot and browser tests. Needs node.

packs.name: lint-tools
packs.about: What aerie lint runs: shellcheck, hadolint, actionlint and ruff, with yq and fd. Without it, aerie lint on a node skips its checks.

packs.name: ffmpeg
packs.about: ffmpeg, ffprobe and ffplay, for cutting, converting and sizing video and audio, and for turning a recording into frames a session can look at.

packs.name: audio
packs.about: What aerie tool sound say and hear run: piper turns text into speech, and whisper turns a recording back into text with its times. About 800 MB.

packs.name: pytorch
packs.about: PyTorch with CUDA, numpy and ONNX, run as python-ml, for training or running a model on the node's NVIDIA card (driver 580 or newer); without a card it runs on the CPU. About 6 GB.

packs.name: graphics
packs.about: What aerie tool graphics runs: ImageMagick for resizing, cropping and comparing images, resvg for SVG to PNG, and oxipng, pngquant and cwebp for shrinking what an app ships.

packs.name: diagrams
packs.about: What aerie tool diagrams runs: PlantUML and Mermaid, diagrams drawn from text. Needs jdk and playwright beside it.

packs.name: documents
packs.about: What aerie tool docs runs: reads a PDF, Word document, slide deck or spreadsheet as Markdown, draws a PDF's pages as pictures, and converts with pandoc. Also lets Claude Code read PDFs. About 650 MB.

packs.name: office
packs.about: What aerie tool office runs: LibreOffice without a window, to turn documents, decks and spreadsheets into PDFs. About 750 MB.

packs.name: ftp
packs.about: The server behind a project's File access setting: FTPS on the project's node, where people sign in with their own AerieOS name and password. About 60 MB.

packs.name: language-servers
packs.about: Python and TypeScript language servers, so a session sees type errors as it edits rather than at the next build.

packs.name: kotlin-lsp
packs.about: JetBrains' Kotlin language server, so a session sees Kotlin errors as it edits. Carries its own Java.

packs.name: rust
packs.about: rustup, cargo and the stable toolchain. Building for Windows also needs a linker: mingw, or zig with cargo-zigbuild.

packs.name: swift
packs.about: The Swift toolchain for Linux: shared logic, server-side Swift, and compiling packages. Not an iOS SDK.

packs.name: zig
packs.about: Zig, and a C and C++ cross-compiler (zig cc) for Windows, macOS and Linux; it also links Rust for those.

packs.name: xcodes
packs.about: Installs and switches Xcode versions on a Mac: run xcodes install --latest on the node, with an Apple ID the first time.

packs.name: claude
packs.about: Claude Code, run by sessions as claude

packs.name: codex
packs.about: Codex CLI, run by sessions as codex

packs.name: copilot
packs.about: Copilot CLI, run by sessions as copilot

packs.name: grok
packs.about: Grok Build, run by sessions as grok

packs.name: open
packs.about: OpenCode, run by sessions as opencode

packs.name: model-router
packs.about: LiteLLM on this node holding your provider keys, Ollama beside it where you turn it on, offered to the spaces you allow: each is handed its address and a key of its own at a session's start, so its spend is its own. What Start's Any model runs through.

packs.name: whoami
packs.about: A tiny web server that answers with the hostname, the address and the headers of the request: the simplest container to prove a deploy with.

packs.name: gemini
packs.about: Gemini: Google's coding agent, Antigravity CLI (agy), as a session's agent, handed the briefing and held by the same guards through its own hooks. Signs in with a Google account in its own terminal.
